openwrt_git.titel: ath79: add support for D-Link DAP-1330/DAP-1365 A1
text: Port device support for DAP-1330 from the ar71xx target to ath79.

Additionally, images are generated for the European through-socket case variant DAP-1365. Both devices run the same vendor firmware, the only difference being the DAP_SIGNATURE field in the factory header. The vendor's Web UI will display a model string stored in the flash.
Specifications: QCA9533, 8 MiB Flash, 64 MiB RAM; One Ethernet Port (10/100); Wall-plug style case (DAP-1365 with additional socket); LED bargraph RSSI indicator
Installation: Web UI: http://192.168.0.50 (or different address obtained via DHCP), There is no password set by default
Recovery Web UI: Keep reset button pressed during power-on until LED starts flashing red, upgrade via http://192.168.0.50

Some modern browsers may have problems flashing via the Web UI, if this occurs consider booting to recovery mode and flashing via: curl -F files=@openwrt-ath79-generic-dlink_dap-1330-a1-squashfs-factory.bin http://192.168.0.50/cgi/index
The device will use the same MAC address for both wired and wireless interfaces, however it is stored at two different locations in the flash.
D-Link DAP-1330 rev. A1 is a wall-plug N300 Wi-Fi range extender, based on Qualcomm/Atheros QCA9533 v2.
650/393/216 MHz (CPU/DDR/AHB)
1x 10/100 Mbps Ethernet
64 MB of RAM (DDR1)
8 MB of FLASH
2T2R 2.4 GHz
2x external antennas
6x LED (2 are bi-color), 2x button
4 pin on pcb (looking from eth port and from left to right tx,rx,gnd,vcc)
Flash instruction: use "factory" image directly in vendor GUI.

Recovery: assigns ip of env serverip via dhcp to a pc, ipaddr to itself; triggered by a not bootable firmware or pressing the reset button during the bootloader startup (first 30 seconds); http page, checks firmware image header (use factory image)
Vendor firmware over serial: login root, password linuxrocks
Image was tested only in EU version of the device

zusatz_zum_commit: Factory image generation is based on mkdapimg2 from ar71xx
LED naming is a little awkward, but compatible to ar71xx.
Apparently using a .dtsi is currently the best method to include identical devices which only differ in the model name.

s-2 2020-05-15: rote RSSI-LED (rssilow) schaltete mit rssileds nur sporadisch; Konfiguration wie Herstellerverhalten belassen (amber statt rot für niedrigsten Bereich)
s-2 2020-05-15: red colour reserved for failsafe and upgrade modes
s-2 2020-05-16: Fehler, dass beide Factory-Images mit DAP1365-Signatur gebaut wurden, behoben (DEVICE_VARS)
s-2 2020-05-14: flashing from ar71xx worked (SUPPORTED_DEVICES), aber mit behaltenen Einstellungen keine Verbindung (nur DAP-1330 betroffen, DAP-1365 gab es in ar71xx nicht)
